options.text: A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force
A wire gets hot when current flows through it
A magnet produces an electric current when it spins
A magnetic field is created around a permanent magnet

questions.explanation: The motor effect states that when a current-carrying conductor is placed in a magnetic field, it experiences a force. This force is perpendicular to both the current direction and the field direction.

questions.stem: In Fleming's left-hand rule, what does the first finger represent?
questions.explanation: In Fleming's left-hand rule: the First finger represents the Field direction (N to S), the seCond finger represents the Current direction (+ to -), and the thuMb represents the direction of Motion (force).

questions.stem: A wire carrying 5 A is placed in a 0.4 T magnetic field. The length of wire in the field is 0.2 m. What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: Using F = BIL: F = 0.4 x 5 x 0.2 = 0.4 N. The force is calculated by multiplying the magnetic flux density, current, and length of wire in the field.

questions.stem: When is the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field zero?

options.text: When the current is very large
When the wire is parallel to the magnetic field
When the magnetic field is very strong
When the wire is perpendicular to the field

questions.explanation: The force on the wire is zero when the wire is parallel to the magnetic field. The force is maximum when the wire is perpendicular to the field.

questions.stem: What is the unit of magnetic flux density?
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux density (B) is measured in tesla (T). One tesla is a very strong field; Earth's magnetic field is only about 50 microtesla.

questions.stem: How can the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field be increased?

options.text: By increasing the current, increasing the field strength, or increasing the length of wire in the field
By making the wire parallel to the field

questions.explanation: From F = BIL, the force increases when any of the three factors increases: stronger magnetic field (B), larger current (I), or longer wire in the field (L).

questions.stem: What is the role of the commutator in a simple DC motor?

options.text: To increase the current flowing through the coil
To reverse the current direction in the coil every half turn, maintaining continuous rotation
To reduce friction in the motor

questions.explanation: The commutator reverses the direction of current in the coil every half turn. Without it, the forces on the coil would reverse after half a rotation, causing the coil to oscillate rather than rotate continuously.
